title: Abelian Ext map in the common section-complex diagram
statement: For a scheme morphism f:X -> Y [def-pc-scheme], module F on X [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], any identity h-map resolution data D=(I,J,K,lambda,beta,a) [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], and natural degree p, let bI,bJ be the explicit abelianResolutionIso of [new-module-cohomology-ext-resolution-normalization]. Let v be exact inverse image on abelian Ext followed by coeff(f,identity), with constIso(f).symm [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison]. Then bJ followed by H(section(beta)) equals v followed by bI and H(a followed by section(lambda)), as morphisms into H(section(K)). This is an equality of abelian Ext/section homology maps. It contains neither the fixed module/Ext equivalence nor the module edge map and does not assume acyclicity of f_*F.

source.place: Tag 01FB, common section diagram; Tag 01F7, canonical cohomology functoriality; Tag 03FD, forgotten injective acyclicity.

proof.text: Forget I,J,K and the compatible augmentations. Forgotten injective modules are acyclic for abelian sections on every open, so forgotten I computes derived abelian direct image. Use the canonical acyclic comparisons to identify abelian Ext with section homology.

The lift beta computes the morphism into the derived abelian direct image. Derived adjunction evaluated on the constant integer source identifies this with inverse image on Ext followed by the counit; terminal evaluation at 1 gives constIso(f).symm. The terminal section map is D.a by D.sections. Thus the common section diagram gives the asserted square.
Naturality of acyclic comparisons and homotopy invariance remove resolution and lift choices.
